newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. soldier held for setting another GI on fire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soldier held for setting another GI on fire.

text.p: A U.S. soldier was in custody on Thursday after he allegedly set a fellow soldier on fire at an American base in southwest Germany.

The suspect, Army Specialist Elisha Green, has been charged with attempted murder in Monday's attack on Specialist Donnel Blackwell at a base in Miesau, Major Bruce Schearer of the 21th Theater Army Area Command said.

Blackwell, a 26-year-old from Washington, D.C., was flown to Brooke Army Medical Centre in San Antonio, Texas, on Monday for treatment of third degree burns over 50 percent of his body, Schearer added.

The incident happened on Monday morning at a base gymnasium. Green is alleged to have thrown flammable liquid over Blackwell before setting him alight. Another soldier grabbed a fire extinguisher to put out the blaze.
Seven soldiers who tried to help Blackwell were also taken to a local military hospital for treatment of smoke inhalation.
Military officials declined to discuss the incident.
But the Stars & Stripes, the unofficial U.S. military newspaper, said the incident was linked to an affair one of the soldiers was allegedly having with the other's wife.
"This is a heinous incident," Schearer said. "Things like this do not happen very often in the military."
Two sergeants were convicted in June of sex-related crimes against younger female soldiers under their command at a training facility in Darmstadt.
A soldier stationed in Germany was also convicted in 1994 after he hacked off the head of his wife's lover and then carried the head in a sports bag to a hospital where his wife was being treated.
